songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Blistering ’67 set with soaring Viola Lee and marathon Alligator > Caution
ai_show_review.blurb: The show erupts with a ferocious 15‑minute Viola Lee Blues, then rolls through tight Pigpen organ work, an epic Alligator > Caution stretch and an ecstatic Other One. Jerry’s razor‑sharp guitar and Phil’s booming bass cut through crystal‑clear soundboard audio.
ai_show_review.review: On November 10, 1967 at the Shrine Exposition Hall in Los Angeles, the Dead delivered a quintessential late‑summer ’67 performance that still feels fresh. The set opens with a blistering, 15‑minute “Viola Lee Blues” where Jerry’s Les Paul tone roars and Pigpen’s organ shouts, then slides into a soulful “It Hurts Me Too” before the band launches into a tight run of classics – “Beat It On Down The Line,” “Morning Dew,” and “Good Morning Little School Girl.” The centerpiece is the marathon “Alligator > Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)” sequence, bolstered by Mickey’s congas and the twin‑drummer interplay that drives the groove into a volcanic climax. Pigpen’s organ/harmonica/vocals shine throughout, especially on “The Other One,” which bursts into an ecstatic, acid‑voice jam. The entire performance is captured on a crystal‑clear soundboard tape that balances Jerry’s searing leads, Phil’s walking bass and the dual‑drum attack with remarkable fidelity, making this one of the most vivid snapshots of the band’s early psychedelic ascent.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture with excellent mix, minimal noise and the full set presented without drops – it showcases the band’s peak ’67 energy.

key_highlights: Ferocious 15‑minute “Viola Lee Blues” that sets a volcanic tone.
Epic “Alligator > Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)” with tight twin‑drummer dynamics.
Pigpen’s organ and vocal performance shines on “The Other One” and “Good Morning Little School Girl”.
Crystal‑clear SBD audio lets every instrument be heard, from Jerry’s razor‑sharp guitar to Phil’s prominent walking bass.

band_performance.Jerry: Fierce, razor‑sharp Les Paul tone with incendiary solos on Viola Lee, Morning Dew and The Other One; rapid‑fire licks drive the Alligator jam.
band_performance.Phil: Walking bass is clear, prominent and more aggressive than earlier in ’67, providing a solid backbone throughout.
band_performance.Bob: Pigpen delivers classic organ work, holds his own amidst the high‑energy set, and adds magical vocals on Good Morning Little School Girl and Caution.
band_performance.Mickey: Tight, complementary drumming with dueling dynamics that shine especially during the Alligator > Caution sequence; congas add texture.
band_performance.Billy: Solid drum foundation that locks in with Mickey, delivering a powerful rhythmic push throughout the marathon jams.
